key_insight: Grouping heterogeneous IoT temperature sensors into Communities of Interest (CoIs) using a fused similarity matrix enables community-based model sharing that improves anomaly detection generalisation across devices.
problem_solved: Scales anomaly detection across large, heterogeneous sensor networks by addressing sensor variability, distribution shift, and the difficulty of building one-size-fits-all models without heavy centralisation or per-device labelling.
method: Compute a fused similarity matrix that combines multiple sensor relationships (e.g., spatial, temporal, operational) to identify Communities of Interest (CoIs).
Cluster sensors into CoIs and share/transfer anomaly detection models within each community rather than using a single global model.
Detect anomalies locally using community-adapted models, improving generalisation across similar devices while limiting unnecessary model sharing.
impact: Enables scalable, privacy-conscious anomaly detection for IoT networks by promoting targeted model reuse and better cross-device generalisation, reducing labeling and central-training burdens for ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Matrix-to-clusters diagram: fused similarity matrix shown transforming into clustered CoIs (heatmap → colored blocks).
Map or floorplan with sensors colored by community to illustrate spatial/operational grouping.
Pipeline flowchart: data → similarity fusion → community clustering → model sharing → anomaly detection.
Performance comparison bar/line chart showing improved detection/generalisation for community-shared models vs single global or per-device baselines.
paper_title: Community-Based Model Sharing and Generalisation: Anomaly Detection in IoT Temperature Sensor Networks
paper_authors: Sahibzada Saadoon Hammad, Joaquín Huerta Guijarro, Francisco Ramos, Michael Gould Carlson, Sergio Trilles Oliver
